generation.embedding_text:
Be succinct yet provide comprehensive detail. Use your experience at least five everyday public systems that have worked with. Be creative. The everyday public system I will choose to explain is the public transportation system, specifically the London Underground Rail System in London, England.

The London Underground Rail System, also known as the Tube, is a comprehensive underground transportation network primarily made up of underground lines connecting various parts of Greater London and a few stations within the geographical limits of other urban areas immediately surrounded by central London. With its rich history dating back to 1863, the Tube system consists of 11 lines with 270 stations.

Upon boarding the train, passengers utilize the fare gates equipped with either traditional Oyster card cards or contactless payment options (i.e., bank cards, mobile contactless) to enter the stations with pre-purchased fare credits or to add money instantly onto one of the two options via automated machines called Oyster card Ticket Machines (OTMs) found in various locations. If traveling outside zones 1-9 within London, travelers will purchase the day ticket for convenience and to take advantage of reduced overall transportation costs.

Passengers may also benefit from the use of maps displayed both online and throughout
